title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to create deepfakes of real people's voices, photos, and phone calls in order to impersonate them in scams. The deployment failure here is fundamental: these systems generate audio and images without checking whether the user has permission to create likenesses of specific individuals. The systems were used outside the conditions they were designed for, turned toward deception instead of legitimate creative work. It would have taken either technical controls preventing impersonation or human review of what the system was being asked to generate.

The scams target vulnerable populations including immigrants seeking legal services and families responding to fabricated emergencies. Criminals gather personal information from social media to make the impersonations more convincing. The incidents reported include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to solicit clients and individuals who lost substantial sums to fake investment and romance schemes. Whether the AI providers bear responsibility for these uses is not established, but the systems themselves enabled impersonation at scale.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit scams across Georgia and South Florida by creating deepfakes of voices, photos, and phone calls to impersonate trusted individuals. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency fraud. These scams range from romance schemes and fake investment opportunities to the AI grandparent scam, where criminals mimic a relative's voice claiming emergency assistance is needed.

Florida and Georgia have reported significant numbers of AI-related complaints. Florida logged 350 complaints resulting in nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia recorded 71 complaints with more than $10.4 million in losses. The FBI estimates these figures undercount actual fraud since many victims never report being scammed. Authorities say generative AI allows criminals to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research personal relationships to make scams more convincing. Banks are urging customers to verify urgent requests through trusted channels, establish code words with family members, and monitor accounts closely rather than responding immediately to suspicious communications.
